text: What is Hugging Face best known for?
options: A repository for sharing models and datasets
A GPU architecture sold to data centres
A web browser used to scrape training data
A cloud provider for GPU workloads
answer: A repository for sharing models and datasets
explanation: The Hub, plus the Transformers library, which is the default way most people load a pretrained model. It is the closest thing the field has to a package registry for weights, and its acquisition by Nvidia in August 2026 made the governance of open model infrastructure a much bigger conversation than it was.

text: Open weights means what exactly?
options: The training data is published alongside the model
The learned parameters are publicly released
The model code is released without a licence
The model may be used without attribution
answer: The learned parameters are publicly released
explanation: The weights and biases, so anyone can download and run them, and whether you can modify, fine tune or redistribute them depends on the licence. That last clause is the whole argument, since a model with open weights and a restrictive licence is not open source by anyone's definition.

text: PyTorch was originally developed at which company?
explanation: Meta, as a successor to Torch, and it is now developed with support from the Linux Foundation. The defining design choice is autograd, where you write forward code and the backward pass is derived for you, which is why PyTorch won over TensorFlow for research work despite TensorFlow arriving first.

text: Under which licence is TensorFlow released?
explanation: The Apache Licence 2.0, which allows commercial use and includes an explicit patent grant. PyTorch uses a similarly permissive BSD style licence, and the permissive choice is the norm for deep learning frameworks because companies want to build on them without a legal review slowing them down.

text: EleutherAI was formed in 2020 with a specific goal. What was it?
options: To create an open source version of GPT-3
To build a public search index for AI papers
To run a public cloud GPU cluster
answer: To create an open source version of GPT-3
explanation: To open source GPT-3, and it started as a Discord server in 2020 before formally incorporating as a non profit institute in early 2023. It is often described as an open source version of OpenAI, which is a nice phrase and also slightly unfair to both organisations.

text: Common Crawl is best known in AI for what?
options: Hosting an open source large language model
Publishing a large public web archive used as training data
Maintaining a registry of AI model licences
Running a public benchmark for code generation
answer: Publishing a large public web archive used as training data
explanation: A non profit that crawls the web and gives away its archives and datasets, free on AWS if you can pay the storage and compute. It is the backbone of an enormous share of web scale pretraining corpora, and it is also why the copyright questions in this field are as hard as they are.

text: Which organization published the Open Source AI Definition 1.0 in October 2024?
explanation: The OSI released version 1.0 requiring use, study, modify and share freedoms plus disclosure of training-data information. The Free Software Foundation is the tempting miss because it defines free software, but the AI definition process was run by the OSI.

text: Under which license were the BLOOM model weights released in 2022?
explanation: The 176B-parameter BigScience model used RAIL, which grants open access but restricts harmful uses. Apache 2.0 is the tempting miss because BLOOM's source code is Apache-licensed, but the weights themselves sit under RAIL.

text: Which organization created The Pile dataset used to train many open models?
explanation: EleutherAI assembled the 825 GB, 22-subset Pile in 2020 and released it publicly at the end of that year. OpenAI is the tempting miss because GPT models dominate the era, but The Pile was the open community's answer for training GPT-Neo and GPT-J.

text: Who started the llama.cpp project for running large language models locally?
explanation: Gerganov began llama.cpp in March 2023 as pure C and C++ inference, later introducing the GGUF format that Ollama and others built on. Karpathy is the tempting miss because his llama2.c also brought local LLM inference to fame, but it is a separate project.

text: You install a local tool for open models and it asks which model to fetch. Where do the model files come from?
explanation: The Hub is where open model weights get published, which makes it the package registry for AI: install a tool, name a model, and the files come down from there. Hugging Face's own ecosystem list names Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp as tools that pull their models straight from it. That is also why who owns the platform gets treated as infrastructure policy rather than just a business.
answerAliases: models hosted on the Hugging Face Hub

text: Someone says they run Llama locally instead of through a hosted API. What does that change in practice?
options: Your prompts and files never leave your own machine
The model's weights were trained on your own computer
The answers are more accurate than a hosted model's
The model gets a larger context window than a hosted one
answer: Your prompts and files never leave your own machine
explanation: The weights are downloaded once and inference happens on your own hardware, so nothing you type is sent to a provider and it keeps working with the network unplugged. The answers and the context window are exactly what the lab published, because it is the same file. What you buy is control: no per-token bill, and no vendor keeping a log. Fitting the model on the machine at all is a separate trick, storing the weights with fewer bits.

text: What does Ollama give you once it is installed?
options: A hosted model that runs in someone else's data centre
A command that pulls a model and starts it locally
A trained model of its own, ready to fine-tune
A rented GPU cluster, billed by the hour
answer: A command that pulls a model and starts it locally
explanation: Ollama bundles the runtime and the weights behind one name you can pull, so the llama.cpp and GGUF plumbing stays out of sight, and it exposes a local REST API on port 11434 for your own programs to call. It does not train models: the weights come from elsewhere, usually the Hugging Face Hub. That is why it became the default answer to how you just run a model on your own machine.
answerAliases: running and managing large language models on local GPU infrastructure

text: A permissive licence carries only minimal requirements. Which of these does it allow that copyleft does not?
options: Publish your own source code under the same terms
Use the work only for non-commercial research
Use the work with no credit to the original author
Use, modify and ship the work inside a closed product
answer: Use, modify and ship the work inside a closed product
explanation: MIT and Apache 2.0 let you keep your own project closed, asking only for a warranty disclaimer and the notice. Copyleft is the mirror image: the GPL and AGPL require you to publish the source of derivative works, which is why they are described as carrying viral obligations. Model weights follow the same split, with Llama and BLOOM shipping bespoke terms rather than a plain MIT or Apache grant.
answerAliases: minimal requirements on how the software can be used, modified, and redistributed

text: EleutherAI shipped two open GPT-style model families in 2021. One was GPT-Neo. What was the other one?
explanation: GPT-J-6B arrived in June 2021 under Apache 2.0, six billion parameters, and it is the release that made fine-tuning an open model cheap for a small team. BLOOM is the tempting miss because it was the famous open model of the following year, but it came out of the BigScience workshop at 176 billion parameters. GPT-NeoX-20B followed in February 2022, and Pythia came later still.

text: How were the original Llama model's weights distributed in 2023?
options: On a case-by-case basis to researchers under a non-commercial licence
Under the MIT Licence with no restrictions
Under the Apache Licence 2.0 to anyone
answer: On a case-by-case basis to researchers under a non-commercial licence
explanation: The first Llama release in February 2023 gave weights only to approved researchers under a non-commercial restriction, while the inference code shipped under GPLv3. Llama 2, released in July 2023, broadened access but still carried an acceptable use policy. Apache 2.0 and MIT are tempting misses because later open models use them, but the original did not.

text: Why is Llama 2 not considered open source by the Open Source Initiative?
options: Its licence includes an acceptable use policy and user restrictions
It requires a licence fee for commercial use
Its weights are not publicly available
It is released only as an API
answer: Its licence includes an acceptable use policy and user restrictions
explanation: Llama 2's licence restricts use by very large services and by certain fields, and the OSI argues those terms violate the Open Source Definition. Meta still calls Llama open source, which is the openwashing debate. The weights are public and there is no API-only release, so the restriction is the crux.

text: Under which licence was Mistral 7B released in 2023?
explanation: Mistral 7B shipped in September 2023 under Apache 2.0, which is why it could be adopted commercially without a special agreement. MIT and RAIL are tempting misses: RAIL is what BLOOM used, and Apache is the common choice for these releases. The Apache grant also includes a patent licence.

text: Which organisation developed the Falcon family of language models?
options: Technology Innovation Institute in Abu Dhabi
answer: Technology Innovation Institute in Abu Dhabi
explanation: Falcon came out of the Technology Innovation Institute, part of Abu Dhabi's Advanced Technology Research Council, starting in 2023. TII also runs the Noor Arabic model. Mistral and Meta are tempting misses because they are the other big open-weight labs of the same period.

text: What did Ai2 release alongside the OLMo model weights?
options: The training data, code, logs and intermediate checkpoints
answer: The training data, code, logs and intermediate checkpoints
explanation: OLMo's stated goal was reproducibility: Ai2 published the weights plus the data, training and evaluation code, logs, metrics and intermediate checkpoints. That is unusual, since most open-weight releases stop at the weights. The hosted-API option is the tempting miss because it describes a proprietary release.

text: How many parameters did the BLOOM model have?
explanation: BLOOM, released in 2022 by the BigScience workshop, has 176 billion parameters and covers 46 natural languages plus 13 programming languages. The smaller figures are tempting misses because they match other open models of the era, and 405 billion matches Llama 3.1.

text: Under which licence is OpenAI's Whisper released?
explanation: Whisper was released as open-source software in September 2022 under the MIT licence, so it can be used and modified freely, including commercially. Apache 2.0 and RAIL are tempting misses because other open models use them, but Whisper's repo carries MIT.

text: What does llama.cpp let you do with a Llama model?
options: Host it as a paid API
Run inference locally, even on a CPU
Train it from scratch on your own data
Fine-tune it in the cloud only
answer: Run inference locally, even on a CPU
explanation: llama.cpp is an open-source C and C++ reimplementation of Llama inference, and it gained traction because it runs on ordinary CPUs without a GPU. Training and cloud-only fine-tuning are tempting misses because they describe other stages of the pipeline.

text: What is GGUF?
options: A binary file format for storing tensors and metadata
answer: A binary file format for storing tensors and metadata
explanation: GGUF is the binary format introduced by llama.cpp in August 2023 to store both tensors and metadata in one file, and it superseded the older GGML format. It is now the standard way to distribute quantized models for local inference. The training-framework option is the tempting miss because the name sounds like a library.

text: Which statement about GGUF and GGML is correct?
options: They are the same format with different names
GGML is a GPU driver and GGUF is a CPU driver
explanation: GGUF was introduced in August 2023 by the llama.cpp project to replace the older GGML format and keep backward compatibility as new architectures were added. GGML was the original tensor library format. The reversed-order option is the common confusion.

text: What does quantization do to a model?
options: Converts it to a different programming language
Reduces the precision of the weights to save memory
answer: Reduces the precision of the weights to save memory
explanation: Quantization stores weights with fewer bits, which cuts memory use and speeds up inference at the cost of some accuracy. It is what makes a 70-billion-parameter model fit on a laptop. It does not add parameters or data.

text: On which default port does Ollama's local REST API listen?
explanation: Ollama exposes its local REST API on port 11434 by default, which is why client libraries and tools know where to connect. 8080 and 3000 are common web defaults but not Ollama's. The port is configurable but 11434 is the out-of-the-box value.

text: What technique is vLLM built around?
explanation: vLLM's central idea is PagedAttention, which manages the transformer key-value cache in pages like virtual memory, reducing waste and enabling continuous batching. FlashAttention is a tempting miss because it also speeds up attention, but it is a different technique.

text: Which library is the default way most people load a pretrained model?
explanation: The Transformers library from Hugging Face is the standard interface for loading and running pretrained models across frameworks. TensorFlow and PyTorch are the underlying frameworks, not the model-loading layer, which is the common confusion.

text: Which Hugging Face library is used for loading and sharing datasets?
explanation: The datasets library provides a standard way to load, process and share datasets, and it is the companion to Transformers. tokenizers, accelerate and peft are real Hugging Face libraries but they handle other parts of the stack.

text: PyTorch is the successor to which earlier framework?
explanation: PyTorch grew out of Torch, the Lua-based framework, and kept its name as a nod. Caffe, Theano and Chainer are real frameworks of the same era but they are separate lineages.

text: TensorFlow was originally developed at which company?
explanation: TensorFlow was created at Google Brain and released in 2015. Meta is the tempting miss because PyTorch is Meta's, and the two frameworks dominate the field.

text: What is ONNX used for?
options: A standard format for representing machine learning models
answer: A standard format for representing machine learning models
explanation: ONNX defines an open standard for representing trained models so they can move between frameworks and runtimes. Training from scratch and GPU architecture are tempting misses because they describe other layers of the stack.

source.label: Open Neural Network Exchange on Wikipedia

text: What is LangChain mainly used for?
explanation: LangChain is a framework that helps integrate language models into applications such as chatbots and document analysis tools. It does not train models or build hardware, which are tempting misses by association.

text: What is LlamaIndex mainly used for?
options: Ingesting, indexing and querying data for language models
answer: Ingesting, indexing and querying data for language models
explanation: LlamaIndex provides tools and frameworks that let language models ingest, index and query structured and unstructured data. It is often used as the data layer in RAG applications. Vision training and chip manufacturing are tempting misses by shape.

text: What does retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) add to a language model?
options: External documents retrieved at inference time
answer: External documents retrieved at inference time
explanation: RAG retrieves relevant documents and adds them to the prompt before generation, so the model can use domain-specific or updated information without retraining. It reduces hallucinations and avoids costly retraining. More parameters and new algorithms are tempting misses.

text: What is a vector database used for?
options: Storing rows and columns of numbers
Storing embeddings and retrieving similar ones
answer: Storing embeddings and retrieving similar ones
explanation: A vector database stores embeddings in vector space and implements approximate nearest-neighbour search, so it can find semantically similar records rather than exact matches. That is why it is the usual retrieval layer in RAG. Relational storage and static hosting are tempting misses.

text: FAISS was originally developed by which organisation?
explanation: FAISS stands for Facebook AI Similarity Search, so it was built at Meta (Facebook) AI. Google and Microsoft are tempting misses because they also publish similarity-search tools, but FAISS is Meta's.

text: Under which licence is Chroma released?
explanation: Chroma is an open-source vector database released under Apache 2.0. The article notes its headquarters are in San Francisco and that it has been used in RAG studies. MIT and BSD are tempting misses because other vector databases use them.

text: Under which licence is Weaviate released?
explanation: The comparison table lists Weaviate under the BSD 3-Clause licence. Apache 2.0 is the tempting miss because most vector databases in the same table use it, but Weaviate is one of the exceptions.

text: Milvus is a distributed vector database developed by which company?
explanation: Milvus is developed by Zilliz and is an open-source project under the LF AI and Data Foundation, released under Apache 2.0. Meta and Google are tempting misses because they publish other database and AI tools.

text: A model released with open weights but a restrictive licence is best described as what?
explanation: When weights are public but the licence restricts use, the model is source-available rather than open source, which is how Ars Technica re-described Llama. Open source requires the freedoms to use, study, modify and share. Proprietary is too strong because the weights are public.

text: What does the Open Source AI Definition 1.0 require about training data?
options: That it be deleted after training
That it be licensed under GPL
That information about it be disclosed
answer: That information about it be disclosed
explanation: The OSI's Open Source AI Definition 1.0 requires disclosure of training-data information, which is why Llama is argued not to qualify. Deletion and GPL licensing are tempting misses because they confuse data handling with software licences.

text: Who introduced the idea of Model Cards for model reporting?
explanation: Model Cards were proposed in a 2019 paper by Mitchell and colleagues to document model performance, intended use and limitations. Timnit Gebru is the tempting miss because she led the related Datasheets for Datasets work.

source.label: Model Cards for Model Reporting on arXiv

text: A model card typically documents which of the following?
explanation: A model card records how the model performs, what it is intended for and where it can fail, so users can decide whether it fits their use. Training bills and star counts are tempting misses because they are easy to measure but not part of the card.

source.label: Model Cards for Model Reporting on arXiv

text: Groq's LPU is best described as what?
options: An AI accelerator chip for inference
answer: An AI accelerator chip for inference
explanation: Groq builds an AI accelerator originally called a Tensor Streaming Processor and later rebranded as a Language Processing Unit for inference. The xAI chatbot Grok is the name-collision trap, since the two are unrelated companies.

text: BLOOM was created by which research effort?
explanation: BLOOM came out of the BigScience workshop, a volunteer-driven research effort to build a transparent alternative to proprietary models. EleutherAI is the tempting miss because it ran a similar open effort, but BLOOM is BigScience's.

text: The Falcon language models were developed in which country?
explanation: Falcon came out of the Technology Innovation Institute in Abu Dhabi, in the United Arab Emirates. France and the United States are tempting misses because other open-weight labs are based there.

text: OLMo was developed by which organisation?
explanation: OLMo is built by the Allen Institute for AI, abbreviated Ai2, as an open and reproducible language model. OpenAI and Meta are tempting misses because they dominate the model landscape, but OLMo is Ai2's project.

text: Stable Diffusion is the premier product of which company?
explanation: Stable Diffusion is the premier product of Stability AI, developed with researchers from LMU Munich and Runway. OpenAI and Midjourney are tempting misses because they are the other image-generation names people remember.

text: Whisper was created by which organisation?
explanation: Whisper is a speech recognition model created by OpenAI and first released as open-source software in September 2022. Meta and Google are tempting misses because they also publish speech models, but Whisper is OpenAI's.

text: vLLM was originally developed at which lab?
explanation: vLLM started at UC Berkeley's Sky Computing Lab, built around PagedAttention. Stanford and MIT are tempting misses because they are associated with other inference and systems work, but vLLM is Berkeley's.

text: Which statement best distinguishes LangChain from LlamaIndex?
options: LangChain is for hardware design, LlamaIndex is for datasets
LangChain builds applications around models, LlamaIndex focuses on ingesting and querying data
LangChain is a database, LlamaIndex is a model
answer: LangChain builds applications around models, LlamaIndex focuses on ingesting and querying data
explanation: LangChain is a general framework for wiring language models into applications, while LlamaIndex specialises in connecting models to data sources. They are often used together. Calling one a database or the other identical are the common confusions.

text: When was the term retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) introduced?
explanation: RAG was introduced in a 2020 paper combining a parametric language model with a non-parametric external memory. 2017 is the tempting miss because that is the transformer year, and 2022 is when RAG became widely adopted.

text: What does FAISS stand for?
options: Fast Approximate Index for Semantic Search
explanation: FAISS stands for Facebook AI Similarity Search, which is why it is often associated with Meta. The other expansions sound plausible but are invented distractors shaped like real acronyms.

text: Chroma is headquartered in which city?
explanation: Chroma's headquarters are in San Francisco. New York and London are tempting misses because other AI infrastructure companies are based there, but Chroma is a San Francisco company.

text: The Open Source Definition prohibits open-source licences from discriminating against what?
options: Persons or groups and fields of endeavour
answer: Persons or groups and fields of endeavour
explanation: The OSI's Open Source Definition bars licences that discriminate against persons or groups or fields of endeavour, which is why Llama's acceptable use policy is disputed. Company size and country are tempting misses because Llama's policy restricts those, but they are not the OSD's categories.

text: Who introduced the GGUF file format?
options: Georgi Gerganov and the llama.cpp community
answer: Georgi Gerganov and the llama.cpp community
explanation: GGUF was introduced in August 2023 by the llama.cpp project, led by Georgi Gerganov, to replace the older GGML format. OpenAI, Google and Meta are tempting misses because they are the big model labs, but GGUF came from the local-inference community.

text: What is the trade-off when quantizing a model?
options: Higher memory use for better accuracy
Lower memory use but some loss of accuracy
answer: Lower memory use but some loss of accuracy
explanation: Quantization reduces precision in the weights, which cuts memory use and speeds up inference at the cost of some accuracy. Higher memory use is the reverse of what happens, and more parameters are not involved.

text: Which of these is a Hugging Face library for tokenization?
explanation: The tokenizers library provides fast text tokenization and is one of Hugging Face's core tools. transformers, datasets and accelerate are real companion libraries but they handle model loading, data and training speed respectively.

text: Which feature does vLLM support for serving many requests?
explanation: vLLM supports continuous batching, which adds new requests to a batch as slots free up, improving throughput. Single-request mode and offline training are tempting misses because they describe other workloads.

text: Under which licence is llama.cpp released?
explanation: llama.cpp is released under the MIT licence. Apache 2.0 is the tempting miss because the models it runs often use Apache, but the inference library itself is MIT.

text: ONNX was originally named what?
explanation: ONNX was originally called Toffee before being renamed in September 2017. Caffe and Tensor are tempting misses because they are real machine-learning names, but neither was ONNX's first name.

text: ONNX's container format is what?
explanation: ONNX uses Protocol Buffers as its container format. JSON and XML are tempting misses because they are common serialisation formats, but ONNX's graphs are stored as protobuf.

source.title: Open Neural Network Exchange
source.label: Open Neural Network Exchange on Wikipedia

text: Which vector database listed in the comparison table is a proprietary managed service?
explanation: The comparison table lists Pinecone as proprietary (managed service), while Milvus, Qdrant and Chroma are open source. Milvus is the tempting miss because it sounds like a managed cloud product, but it is open source.

text: Which licence is often associated with open weights models that are not open source?
explanation: RAIL licences grant access to weights but restrict harmful uses, which is why BLOOM is open access but not open source by the OSI's definition. MIT and Apache are tempting misses because they are the permissive licences used by fully open source projects.

text: What is the difference between open weights and open source?
options: Open weights releases the learned parameters; open source also grants the freedoms to use, study, modify and share
Open weights requires a paid licence; open source is free
Open weights includes the training data; open source does not
answer: Open weights releases the learned parameters; open source also grants the freedoms to use, study, modify and share
explanation: Open weights means the parameters are public, but whether you can modify, fine-tune or redistribute them depends on the licence. Open source adds the freedoms to use, study, modify and share. The training-data and paid-licence options are tempting misses because they confuse weights with data and cost.

text: Qdrant, the open-source vector search engine, is written in which programming language?
explanation: Qdrant's own README says it is written in Rust, which is what keeps it fast and reliable under high load. Go, Python and TypeScript are the tempting misses because Qdrant ships official clients in all three, but clients are not the engine.

text: In Ollama, what is a Modelfile?
options: The GGUF weight file downloaded from the model library
The blueprint file for creating and sharing customized models
The local REST API listening on port 11434
The llama.cpp backend that runs local inference
answer: The blueprint file for creating and sharing customized models
explanation: A Modelfile holds FROM, PARAMETER, SYSTEM and similar instructions that define how a model is built and run, so sharing the file shares the customization. The GGUF weights, the port-11434 API and the llama.cpp backend are all real parts of Ollama's stack, which is exactly why they tempt, but none of them is the Modelfile.

text: vLLM is an open-source framework for what?
options: Distributed training of foundation models from scratch
Versioning datasets for machine learning pipelines
Inference and serving of large language models
Scraping web text for pretraining corpora
answer: Inference and serving of large language models
explanation: vLLM is a serving engine built around PagedAttention and continuous batching, designed for high-throughput inference. Training from scratch is the tempting miss because that is what frameworks in the DeepSpeed family do, while dataset versioning and web scraping belong to other tools entirely.
answerAliases: inference and serving of large language models

text: When llama.cpp began in March 2023, whose inference code was it implementing?
explanation: Gerganov wrote llama.cpp as a pure C and C++ reimplementation of the Llama inference code so the model could run on an ordinary CPU with no GPU. GPT, PaLM and Claude tempt because every lab has a flagship model, but in March 2023 only Meta's weights were available to build a local runner around.
